chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub said: Ali ibn Muhammad, who elevated it (to the Imam), from Muhammad ibn al-Faraj al-Rukhji, said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)

asking him about what Hisham ibn al-Hakam said regarding the body, and Hisham ibn Salim regarding the image. So he (peace be upon him) wrote to me: Leave aside the confusion of the bewildered, and seek refuge in Allah from Satan. The statement is not as the two Hishams claimed.

key_terms.الهشامان: The two Hishams (referring to Hisham ibn al-Hakam and Hisham ibn Salim)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Kadhim say about the views of Hisham ibn al-Hakam and Hisham ibn Salim regarding God's body and image?
ai.summary: In this narration from *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Rida (AS) refutes the specific anthropomorphic views of Hisham ibn al-Hakam and Hisham ibn al-Salim regarding divine 'body' (jism) and 'image' (surah), affirming the Imami doctrine of God's transcendence beyond physical form. By instructing the seeker to 'leave aside the confusion of the confused,' the Imam distinguishes the precise theological nuance of the Ahl al-Bayt from broader sects, emphasizing that God is devoid of both material composition and perceptible shape. This hadith serves as a critical reference for Shia kalām, reinforcing the concept of *tanzih* (divine transcendence) against *tashbih* (anthropomorphism).
